subject: Biotechnology
title: Biological Pest Control
description: Learn Biological Pest Control in one minute.

hook.text: Release engineered sterile insects — they mate with wild pests but produce no offspring. Population crashes.

buildup.text: The sterile insect technique irradiates male insects — released in millions, they outcompete wild males.

discovery.text: Oxitec's modified mosquitoes carry a self-limiting gene — their offspring inherit a lethal gene and die before adulthood.

twist.text: Wolbachia bacteria make male mosquitoes infertile when mating with wild females — no genetic modification needed.

climax.text: Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes reduced dengue cases by 77% in a city-wide trial in Yogyakarta, Indonesia.

punchline.text: Fight pests with biology, not chemicals — engineered insects reshape pest control.

quiz.question: How do Oxitec's modified mosquitoes reduce pest populations?
options: They release a toxin that kills other mosquitoes on contact
Their offspring inherit a self-limiting gene that causes death before adulthood
They eat the larvae of wild mosquitoes in breeding sites

details.summary: Biological pest control uses living organisms like predators, parasitoids, and microbial agents to manage crop pests instead of chemical pesticides. Biotech advances enable engineering more effective biocontrol agents and optimizing their deployment in agriculture.
details.whyItMatters: Chemical pesticides harm ecosystems and human health. Biological control offers targeted, environmentally friendly pest management that reduces chemical inputs while maintaining crop yields and supporting biodiversity.
takeaways: Biocontrol uses natural enemies like predatory insects and microbes
Bacillus thuringiensis is the most successful microbial biocontrol agent
Integrated pest management combines biocontrol with minimal chemical use

faq.question: How does Bacillus thuringiensis control pests?
faq.answer: Bt produces crystal proteins toxic to specific insect groups when ingested. The toxins punch holes in the insect gut lining, killing the pest within days. Different Bt strains target different insects, allowing precise pest control without harming beneficial species.

faq.question: Can biocontrol agents become invasive species?
faq.answer: Yes, poorly chosen biocontrol agents have caused ecological damage historically. Modern biocontrol programs conduct extensive host-specificity testing before release to ensure agents target only the intended pest and do not harm native species.
